name: Tennis rules summary
summary: Two players, or two pairs, hit the ball over a net and try to make it land in the opposite court so the other side cannot return it before a second bounce. Points build into games, games into sets, and a match is the best of three or five sets.

points.text: The server starts at rest with both feet behind the baseline, between the imaginary extensions of the centre mark and the sideline, releases the ball by hand and hits it before it lands
The serve must clear the net and land in the service court diagonally opposite
In a standard game the server alternates halves of the court, beginning from the right half in every game
After a fault on the first serve the server serves again, without delay, from the same half
A serve that clips the net and still lands in the correct service court is a let and is taken again; it does not count as a fault
Points in a standard game run love, 15, 30, 40, game; at 40-40 (deuce) a player must win two points in a row, the first being advantage
In a tie-break set the first to six games with a two-game lead wins; at six games all a tie-break game is played
In an advantage set play continues until one side leads by two games
A tie-break game is scored 0, 1, 2, 3 and so on; the first to seven points with a two-point lead takes the game and the set
A match is the best of three sets or the best of five
The rules also allow alternative methods such as no-advantage games, short sets and a match tie-break in place of a final set
A ball that touches any part of a line counts as landing in the court that line bounds
A player loses the point if the ball bounces twice on their side before they return it, or if their return lands outside the correct court
A return that touches the net, posts, cord, strap or band and then lands in the correct court is good
A player loses the point if they, their racket or anything they wear or carry touches the net or the opponent's court while the ball is in play

It is a foot fault if the server, during the service motion, moves position by walking or running, or touches the baseline, the court, or the imaginary extension of the sideline or centre mark with either foot
points.editorNote: Widened on 2026-10-24 to include the imaginary extensions (Rule 18(c) and (d))

points.text: A serve is a fault if the server breaks the position or foot-fault rules, misses the ball when trying to hit it, or the served ball hits a net post, a singles stick or any other fixed object before landing
Two faults in a row (a double fault) lose the point
A player hindered by a deliberate act of the opponent wins the point; an unintentional hindrance or one outside the player's control means the point is replayed

The pair serving first decides which partner serves the first game; the opposing pair then decides who serves the second game, and service rotates through all four players in that order for the rest of the set
The receiving pair decides which partner receives the first point, and partners then receive alternately; the order stays the same for the whole set
Doubles is played on the wider court, 10.97 m across instead of 8.23 m for singles
points.editorNote: Reworded on 2026-10-24: the rulebook gives the widths rather than naming the alleys
